CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — an author that did not
resolve cannot be shown to be somebody else, so self-review is not ruled out

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — GitHub logins are
case-insensitive, so capitalising one is the same account

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — surrounding whitespace
names the same account

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — `str.strip()` does not
remove U+200B, so an invisible author is non-blank and names nobody

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — U+FEFF survives
`str.strip()` for the same reason U+200B does

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — a control character is
not whitespace and identifies no account

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — an author with no
alphanumeric character names nobody a human can check, so the identity
is unresolved rather than merely unequal to the PR's

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — `@login` is how a
hand-written capture ordinarily spells a login, and `@` is not a
character a GitHub login contains, so the string is no login and
names nobody — self-review is not ruled out

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — sentence punctuation is
not part of a login, so `nuncaeslupus.` is not one and names nobody

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — brackets are not login
characters, so a parenthesised login is not a login

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — U+FF41..U+FF5A are not
the ASCII letters a login is drawn from. Round 4 NFKC-folded them
back; round 5 removed that fold because the same fold turns `™`
into the identity `tm`, so the spelling now names nobody instead

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — a GitHub login holds no
space, so a spaced spelling is not a login and names nobody

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — a login may neither begin
nor end with a hyphen, so `- nuncaeslupus` is not one

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — a login may neither
begin nor end with a hyphen, so a string of them is no login at all
and names nobody a human can check

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — `gh` prints the author
association beside the login, and round 4 welded it on as
`nuncaeslupusowner`, an identity that is not the author's and cleared
the head at exit 0. A badge is not part of a login, so the string is
not one

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — brackets are outside the
alphabet and `bot` is inside it, so round 4 welded `nuncaeslupusbot`

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — the worst shape of the
weld: `nuncaeslupus-maintainer` is a WELL-FORMED login that no account
bears, so nothing downstream could tell it was manufactured

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — U+00B2 is not an ASCII
digit; NFKC rewrote it into the identity `2`, which named a second
reader that does not exist

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — NFKC LENGTHENS U+2167
into `VIII`, which is the counterexample to round 4's claim that the
transform only ever merges

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — `™` became `tm`, a login
shape a human would read as an account and could not find

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — a circled letterform is
presentation, and folding it produced the identity `a`

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — `½` folds to a digit, a
FRACTION SLASH and a digit; the slash is then deleted, welding the
identity `12`: a rewrite and a weld in one character
CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — `㎏` folds to `kg`

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — the mirror of #31. The
author welded to `nuncaeslupusowner`, so their own marker read as a
second reader's and cleared the head at exit 0

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — the mirror of #32, and
the direction that matters: a decorated AUTHOR field is what lets the
author be somebody else

rewrote `™` into the identity `tm` and answered `allowed/0` over a PR
whose author it had invented

t-41fda10d: the author-side mirror of #26. It was already fail-closed
under round 4 (folded to the same account, `blocked/2`) and stays
fail-closed here for a different reason — a fullwidth spelling is not
a login. Committed so the AUTHOR side has a control either way

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — casefold survives the
validator, on the AUTHOR side too: GitHub logins are case-insensitive

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: a PR may merge once a session other than its implementer has
read it — digits are in the login grammar and must not be refused

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: a login may begin with a digit, so `^[A-Za-z0-9]` and not
`^[A-Za-z]` — a validator that refused this would block real readers

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: a PR may merge once a session other than its implementer has
read it — outer whitespace is transport framing, not identity, and it
is the one thing `str.strip()` may still remove because it cannot weld

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: a PR may merge once a session other than its implementer has
read it — the hyphen IS in the login alphabet, so `nunca-es-lupus` is
a different account from `nuncaeslupus` and this control is the one
that stops the round-4 fold from merging two real people into one
